title: A protocol to quantify protein copy number in super-resolution using DNA Origami as a calibration standard
protocol: Fold the 12-helix bundle DNA origami chassis structures in folding buffer by mixing 100 nM p8064 scaffold with 600 nM core staples, 3.6 μM handle staples, 3.6 μM biotin staples, and 9 μM fluorophore anti-handles.
Run the thermal folding cycle involving rapid heating to 80°C followed by cooling in single degree increments to 65°C for 75 min, then further cooling in single degree increments to 30°C for 17.5 hr.
Store folded chassis at either 4°C or -20°C.
Equilibrate Microbiospin6 columns in buffer consisting of 10 mM Tris (pH 8), 150 mM KCl, and 10% v/v glycerol.
Dilute A* antihandle (NH2) to a concentration of 2 mM in water.
Dilute BG-NHS to a concentration of 20 mM in non-aqueous DMSO.
Mix at room temperature for 30 min: 16 μl of 2 mM A* NH2, 32 μl of 200 mM HEPES (pH 8.5), and 48 μl of 2 mM BG-NHS.
Filter the mixture in a 0.1 ultrafree MC durapore membrane centrifuge at 12,000g for 1-4 min.
Purify BG-oligos using MicroBioSpin6 columns by applying 24 μl BG-oligos and centrifuging four times for 1 min each at 1,000g and 4°C.
Store purified BG-oligos at -20°C.

Grind yeast cells diluted in Dynein lysis buffer (30 mM HEPES (pH 7.2), 50 mM KAcetate, 2 mM MgAcetate, 1 mM EGTA, 10% glycerol, 1 mM DTT, 0.5 mM Mg-ATP, 1 mM Pefabloc) and spin for 1 hour at 60K rpm at 4°C.
Incubate the supernatant with equilibrated IgG Sepharose beads and nutate for 1-2 hours at 4°C.
Wash the beads twice with 1X wash buffer.
Wash the beads twice with 1X TEV buffer and incubate them (20 minutes at RT) with BG-oligonucleotides (20 µM).
Wash the beads three times in TEV buffer.
Incubate the beads with TEV protease (1:100 in TEV buffer) for 1 hour at 16°C with rotation.
Remove the beads with centrifugal filters and concentrate the protein with Amikon 100K.
Freeze the concentrated protein in liquid nitrogen.
Store the sample at -80°C.
Prepare coverslip washed with KOH (1M) for 5 minutes.
Rinse the coverslip three times and incubate with 100 µL of BSA-Biotin (0.5mg/ml) for 20 min RT.
Rinse the coverslip three times in miliQ water and incubate with 100 µL Streptavidin (0.5mg/ml) for 20’ RT.
Incubate the coverglass with Carboxyl Fluorescent Particles (Yellow, 1% w/v Spherotec SPH-CFP-0252-2, diameter 111nm at a dilution of 1:30,000) for 10 min.
Block the coverglass in blocking buffer containing 10% (wt/vol) BSA in DAB solution for 10-30 minutes at room temperature.
Mix 2 μL of purified dynein (300 nM) with 2 μL of DNA origami solution (3 nM).
Incubate diluted motor-chassis complexes at a concentration of 30 pM in DAB* blocking buffer for 5’ RT on pre-cleaned and functionalized coverslip.
Rinse gently twice in DAB* blocking buffer at 4°C.
Block with DAB* blocking solution for 15’ at 4°C.
Add primary antibody (chicken polyclonal anti GFP, Abcam 13970) diluted 1:2000 in DAB* blocking buffer and incubate for 1h at 4°C.
Rinse three times in DAB* blocking solution at 4°C.
Add donkey-anti chicken secondary antibody with photoactivatable dye pairs for STORM (A405/A647) diluted 1:50 in DAB* blocking solution and incubate for 1h at 4°C.
Rinse three times in DAB* blocking solution.
Add imaging buffer containing GLOX solution, MEA, and casein.
Set the readout power to the desired power and frame rate.
Set the activation power to ensure sparseness of the imaged molecules.
Image the DNA origami with a fixed routine based on 1 activation frame followed by 3 readout frames.
Acquire until all the molecules are completely bleached.
Change the imaging buffer every 2 hours.
Analyze the DNA Origami data using Least Squares Fitting method.
Set a threshold of 2000 counts for considering a molecule for further analysis.
Exclude spots smaller than 200nm and larger than 500nm from further analysis.
Consider molecules localized in positions closer than 16nm as the same molecule and link them together.
Run the deco.m code.
Load the .txt file of data by clicking the "Load data" button.
Fit the data by clicking the "Fit" button.
Save the results by clicking the "Save output" button.
Simulate expected distribution of stoichiometries using synthetic origami data.
Launch the deco.m code.
Set the "Type of pdf" (LogNormal or Exponential) depending on calibration data.
Set function parameters in deco.m code.
Set N, the "number of pdfs" fn composing your expected distribution.
Check "only even components" if only even functions are needed.
Display calibration functions in the plot on the bottom-left corner of the GUI.
Click the "Simulate" button to generate a window for sample input.
Input the number of samples and values of relative weights wn for n pdfs.
Choose the name and path of the file to be saved after clicking OK.
Fit simulated data using deco.m code.
Compare fitting results with known distribution of monomers/dimers.
Quantify goodness of fit estimator.
Increase the number of sample if data are not satisfactorily fitted.
